title: Ledger and Uniform
premise: In the final winter of the Great War, August Voss, an apprentice clockmaker with a ledger for a heart, is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock and finds a half-starved child abandoned on its steps with a note instructing everyone to forget the face. The child, Lior, carries a stolen ledger of names — deserters, smuggled families, and the last berth on a coastal relief ship departing before the armistice. As August's found family at the observatory fractures over who deserves that berth, August must decide whether to keep measuring the world in what can be carried, or carry someone instead. When the armistice is signed and the ship sails without them, August forges a new entry in the ledger: their own names, staying, becoming the family the note tried to erase.
about_author: Wendell Iversen is a retired horological conservator who spent thirty years restoring tower clocks across northern Europe before turning to fiction. He writes in the margins of maintenance logs, convinced that every mechanism keeps time for someone who cannot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Parts
chapters.summary: August Voss, POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, August catalogs every tool by weight and necessity, revealing a mind that survives by carrying little. Emotional beat: guarded competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Face Instructed to Be Forgotten
chapters.summary: August's POV. On the observatory steps at dawn, August finds a child, Lior, clutching a note: forget the face. The master clockmaker, Halvard, insists they cannot keep it. Emotional beat: the first crack in August's ledger-logic.

chapters.title: Halvard's Hands
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The old clockmaker remembers his own lost son and quietly teaches August the clock's escapement while pretending indifference to Lior. Emotional beat: grief disguised as craftsmanship.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: August's POV. August discovers Lior's stolen ledger: deserters, hidden families, and one final berth on the relief ship Meridian, sailing before the armistice. Emotional beat: dread — the war has entered the tower.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: August's POV. August inventories the observatory household — cook Marta, astronomer's widow Ines, Halvard — measuring who could flee and who could not. Emotional beat: the cold arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Ines Reads the Sky
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The widow charts weather and troop movements by starlight, telling August the armistice may not come when promised. Emotional beat: fragile hope in an unreliable sky.

chapters.title: The Knock at Midnight
chapters.summary: August's POV. A soldier claiming to be Lior's uncle arrives, demanding the child and the ledger; Halvard turns him away with a clockmaker's calm lie. Emotional beat: the family closes ranks, first time as a family.

chapters.title: Marta's Ration Book
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The cook reveals she has been forging ration papers for strangers for a year; the observatory is already a refuge. Emotional beat: August realizes the ledger's names include everyone he loves.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: August's POV. The master clock fails completely; repairing it becomes an allegory August cannot escape — every part must release to keep time. Emotional beat: August admits some things must be let go to function.

chapters.title: The Soldier Returns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The child, who has not spoken, watches the soldier search the town and recognizes him as the man who took their mother's berth. Emotional beat: terror breaking into speech.

chapters.title: Testimony in Small Hours
chapters.summary: August's POV. Lior tells the story of the stolen berth and the note; August understands the uncle wants the ledger to erase his crime. Emotional beat: protective fury — August's first emotion too large for the ledger.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Manifest
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines uses her late husband's naval contacts to verify the berth and learns the ship may sail early, before the armistice. Emotional beat: the clock is running out, literally and morally.

chapters.title: Halvard's Offer
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard secretly arranges for Lior to take the berth, planning to stay behind alone with his clocks. Emotional beat: sacrificial love the old man refuses to name.

chapters.title: Marta Refuses the Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta confronts August: choosing one person is how the war thinks; the family must refuse the ledger's logic. Emotional beat: moral rupture inside the household.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Bargain
chapters.summary: August's POV. The soldier offers August safe passage in exchange for the ledger and the child; August stalls, buying a night. Emotional beat: temptation and self-disgust.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard opens the master clock's case to reveal names scratched inside by his son — the tower has always been a refuge of memory. Emotional beat: inheritance of remembrance over forgetting.

chapters.title: The Night of the Sailing
chapters.summary: August's POV. The household races to the harbor through curfew streets with the soldier in pursuit; the Meridian's gangplank is raised. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, everything carried at once.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. At the gangplank, August must choose who boards: Lior, Halvard, or Marta. August gives the berth to Halvard — the man with the least time left — and lies to the soldier with the ledger's forged page. Emotional beat: the choice that defines him.

chapters.title: Armistice Bells
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The armistice is signed; the observatory's repaired master clock rings the hour as the town erupts. Halvard is gone; the soldier is taken by military police. Emotional beat: relief braided with grief.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger Aloud
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The household reads every name in Lior's ledger aloud at the kitchen table, refusing to forget a single face. Emotional beat: mourning as an act of family.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Mark
chapters.summary: August's POV. August signs his own name beside Halvard's scratched ones inside the clock case and takes up the master clockmaker's tools. Emotional beat: identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: What We Carried
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. A year later, Lior asks what August carried from the war; August answers: everyone. The clock keeps perfect time over a household that stayed. Emotional beat: found family as the truest ledger.
